quandoUsar: Ask permission inside the conversation before an agent runs a tool, showing its name and the exact arguments of the call.
When the person needs three outcomes: allow once, allow always or deny.
Long transcripts: after the decision, the request shrinks to a line that records the answer and can be reopened with “Change”.
quandoEvitar: Use `approval-card` for a business decision with a summary, details as label and value pairs and an “Undo”.
Use `tool-result` to record a call that has already run, with input, output and duration.
Use `dialog` when the decision must block the rest of the screen until it is made.

teclado.acao: Moves through “Deny”, “Always allow” and “Allow once”, in that order.
On a decision button, decides and moves focus to the “Change” of the result line, or to the request itself with `allowChange={false}`.
On “Change”, reopens the request and moves focus to “Allow once”.

acessibilidade: The root is a `role="group"` named “Permission request for” plus the `tool`, and the arguments sit in an “Arguments” group; a truncated value shows the full text in `title`.
When the decision comes from a button in the request, focus goes to the button that replaces it and does not fall to `body`; the result sits in a `role="status"` region.
“Wants to run”, “Permission request for” and “Arguments” are fixed in English; the button and result texts are translated through `labels`.
movimento: On decision, the request leaves upward with a light blur, the result line enters in its place and the frame follows the new height with a spring.
The result icon draws itself: a check mark for allow and a two-stroke X for deny.
With “reduce motion” on, swaps are opacity-only, the height changes instantly and the icons appear already drawn.
responsivo: It is a width container: below 21rem the two allow buttons share one row and “Deny” drops below them, at full width; in the result line, the argument disappears.
notasIA: Pause the agent until `onDecisionChange` returns `once`, `always` or `denied`; the “Always allow” rule is yours, because the component only records the choice.
`args` accepts an object (one `chave: valor` line per field, non-text values as JSON) or a string with line breaks; the result line shows only the first value.
Translate with `labels` (`once`, `always`, `deny`, `allowedOnce`, `allowedAlways`, `denied`, `change`); for history, render already-decided requests with `defaultDecision`.
